facts.heading: Tomas is nervous about therapy
facts.content: Tomas is nervous about attending therapy.
facts.evidence: I am quite nervous, if I am to be honest.

facts.heading: Wife suggested therapy
facts.content: Tomas's wife suggested he attend therapy because she felt things couldn't continue.
facts.evidence: My wife. She says it can't go on like this.

facts.heading: Compulsive checking behavior
facts.content: Tomas checks if he locked the door and turned off the stove thirty times per night.
facts.evidence: Thirty times a night I check if I locked the door and turned off the stove,

facts.heading: Time taken to leave apartment
facts.content: It takes Tomas an hour to leave his apartment.
facts.evidence: it takes me an hour to leave the apartment.

facts.heading: Checking routine details
facts.content: Tomas's routine involves locking the door, going to the elevator, returning to pull the handle, checking the stove knobs separately, and checking the door again.
facts.evidence: I lock the door, I go to the elevator, I come back and pull the handle. Then I check the stove, every knob separately. Then the door again.

facts.heading: Relief followed by anxiety
facts.content: After checking, Tomas feels relieved temporarily, but then an image comes to his head that he didn't do it properly, requiring him to check again.
facts.evidence: I feel relieved for a while. And then an image comes into my head that I didn't do it properly, and I have to do it again.

facts.heading: Fire image appears daily
facts.content: Tomas sees a clear image of the apartment on fire every day.
facts.evidence: The apartment on fire. I see it clearly, like a film.

facts.heading: Anxiety peaks in evenings/mornings
facts.content: The anxiety is worst in the evening when they go out or go to sleep, and also in the morning.
facts.evidence: It's the worst in the evening when we go out or go to sleep. In the morning too.

facts.heading: Fire started two years ago
facts.content: The issue started two years ago.
facts.evidence: It started two years ago when the neighbors' house caught fire and we had to evacuate.

facts.heading: Fire incident triggered issues
facts.content: The problems began after the neighbors' house caught fire, which forced them to evacuate.
facts.evidence: It started two years ago when the neighbors' house caught fire and we had to evacuate.

facts.heading: Experience of fire evacuation
facts.content: Tomas remembers the fire incident where the alarm woke him up, there was smoke, and people were screaming.
facts.evidence: The alarm woke me up. There was smoke in the hallway and people were screaming.

facts.heading: Feeling of personal responsibility
facts.content: Since the fire, Tomas feels he can cause it, and if he doesn't control something, it will happen and he will be to blame.
facts.evidence: Since then I have the feeling that I can cause it. That if I don't control something, it will happen and I will be to blame.

facts.heading: Inability to stop checking
facts.content: Tomas acknowledges the logic but states he cannot stop the checking behavior.
facts.evidence: I know the logic. But I can't turn it off.

facts.heading: Anxiety escalation when resisting
facts.content: When Tomas tries to let the urge go, anxiety grows until he feels like he is going crazy, leading him to prefer the checking.
facts.evidence: And then anxiety grows in me, until I feel like I'm going crazy. I'd rather do it.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of anxiety
facts.content: Tomas experiences heart symptoms, sweating, shaking hands, and stomach sickness when anxious.
facts.evidence: Heart, sweat. My hands shake and I feel sick in my stomach.

facts.heading: Wife is aware of the issue
facts.content: Tomas's wife, Barbora, knows about the issue.
facts.evidence: Barbora. My wife.

facts.heading: Wife's reaction to issue
facts.content: Barbora initially saw the behavior as a habit, but now she recognizes it is more serious.
facts.evidence: At first she took it as a habit, now she sees that it's more.

facts.heading: Late arrival at cinema
facts.content: Tomas arrived forty minutes late to the cinema yesterday.
facts.evidence: Yesterday we arrived at the cinema forty minutes later.

facts.heading: Wife waited for checking
facts.content: Barbora waited outside the cinema for Tomas to return and check the stove for the third time.
facts.evidence: She waited outside for me to return and check the stove for the third time.

facts.heading: Reported feelings of shame
facts.content: Tomas felt shame and felt like a child who cannot leave the house.
facts.evidence: Shame. I felt like a child who can't leave the house.

facts.heading: Job as electrician in Olomouc
facts.content: Tomas works as an electrician in Olomouc. He does wiring in apartments and houses.
facts.evidence: I work as an electrician in Olomouc. I do wiring in apartments and sometimes in houses.

facts.heading: Checking related to work mistakes
facts.content: Tomas checks his work because he is afraid of making a mistake that could cause something to burn.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid that because of my head I will make a mistake once.

facts.heading: Checking behavior after jobs
facts.content: Tomas goes back to check his work after every job, sometimes checking the next day.
facts.evidence: after every job I go back and check. Sometimes I go back the next day, just to look.

facts.heading: Colleagues view Tomas as pedant
facts.content: Tomas's colleagues think he is a pedant.
facts.evidence: They think I'm a pedant.

facts.heading: Boss notes Tomas's carefulness
facts.content: Tomas's boss says he is the most careful in the company.
facts.evidence: The boss tells me I'm the most careful in the company,

facts.heading: Checking adds one hour daily

facts.evidence: In the last few months, it adds an hour to my work per day.

facts.heading: Handed over jobs due to time

facts.evidence: I've already handed over a few jobs to a colleague because I didn't have time.

facts.heading: Fear of losing job
facts.content: Tomas is afraid he will lose his job, especially now.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid I'll lose my job. Especially now.

facts.heading: Barbora is four months pregnant
facts.content: Barbora is four months pregnant.
facts.evidence: Barbora is four months pregnant.

facts.heading: Waited three years for pregnancy
facts.content: Tomas and Barbora waited three years for the pregnancy.
facts.evidence: We waited for it for three years.

facts.heading: Intrusive thoughts of harming family

facts.evidence: That I will harm her and the baby.

facts.content: Tomas fears the thought of harming them might happen while cutting bread or by the stairs.

facts.content: Tomas believes checking helps calm the intrusive thoughts.

facts.heading: Walks twice weekly

facts.evidence: Walks twice a week,

facts.evidence: repairs when there is something.

facts.heading: Goals for future
facts.content: Tomas wants to leave the apartment and look forward to having a child without those thoughts.

facts.heading: Fear of exposure therapy
facts.content: Tomas was afraid of therapy where a person is gradually exposed to what they are afraid of.
facts.evidence: I was afraid of that.
